mainTopic: The end of the bribed-philosopher story, the משנה's ban on reading כתובים on שבת (רב and שמואל), the משנה on rescuing a ספר תורה with its case, and the dispute about skinning the קרבן פסח on שבת.
overview: This amud has three parts. First, it finishes the story of the philosopher who claimed he never took bribes. אימא שלום gave him a golden lamp and won her case, then רבן גמליאל gave him a donkey and the ruling flipped, exposing him. Next, the גמרא explains the משנה's rule that we do not read כתובים on שבת so people will not miss the בית המדרש. רב and שמואל argue about when and where this applies. The גמרא challenges שמואל from the practice in his own town, נהרדעא. It answers in two ways: one by re-stating the dispute, and one through רב אשי, who links שמואל's statement to רבי נחמיה. Then a new משנה allows rescuing a ספר תורה or תפילין from a fire together with their cases. The גמרא brings a ברייתא on how much of the קרבן פסח may be skinned on שבת. It explains both sides and ends with the חכמים' comparison to the ספר תורה casing, which רב אשי explains is about moving the hide along with the meat.

steps.title: The philosopher's reputation and the plan to expose him
steps.stepSummary: The philosopher claimed he never took bribes. אימא שלום and רבן גמליאל plan to show this is false, and she gives him a golden lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: The philosopher spread a reputation that he does not take bribes. They wanted to mock him and expose him. She secretly gave him a golden lamp, and then she and her brother came before him for a court case.
steps.whatsHappening: The story, which began on the previous amud, sets up its scene. The גמרא is preparing us for a test of the philosopher's honesty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The philosopher's whole image rests on refusing bribes. The golden lamp is a secret bribe from אימא שלום, the sister of רבן גמליאל. Watch the lamp, because it comes back in the punchline.

keyTerms.meaning: To mock him, to make a fool of him

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a story. 'She' is אימא שלום, the wife of רבי אליעזר and the sister of רבן גמליאל, who were named on the previous amud.

phrases.english: who had taken on a reputation
phrases.notes: This refers to a philosopher who lived in their neighborhood, introduced on the previous amud.

phrases.english: that he does not accept bribes.
They wanted to mock him.
phrases.notes: The goal was to expose his hypocrisy.

phrases.english: She brought him a golden lamp,
phrases.notes: She gave it to him privately, as a bribe.

phrases.english: and they went before him.
phrases.notes: She and her brother came as if they had a real case to judge.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּהֲוָה שְׁקִיל שְׁמָא דְּלָא מְקַבֵּל שׁוּחְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a story begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The philosopher claims honesty, and a secret bribe is placed to test him.

steps.title: The sister asks for a share of the inheritance and gets it
steps.stepSummary: אימא שלום asks for a share of her father's estate, and the bribed philosopher immediately rules that they should divide it.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: I want a share in the property of my father's house. He said to them: Divide it.
steps.whatsHappening: The bribed judge rules for the person who bribed him. The daughter gets a share even though her brother is alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תורה, a daughter does not inherit when there is a son. The philosopher's quick ruling in her favor is the first sign that the lamp worked.

phrases.english: She said to him: I want
that they give me a share in the property of my father's house.
phrases.notes: She wants to share in the inheritance alongside her brother.

phrases.english: He said to them: Divide it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: בָּעֵינָא דְּנִיפְלְגוּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the first effect of the bribe from Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bribed philosopher rules that the daughter shares the inheritance.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל cites the תורה, and the philosopher says it was replaced
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל objects that the תורה says a daughter does not inherit where there is a son. The philosopher answers that the תורה was replaced by the עוון גליון, which says son and daughter inherit equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to him: It is written in our תורה that where there is a son, the daughter does not inherit. The philosopher said: Ever since you were exiled from your land, the תורה of משה was taken away and the עוון גליון was given instead. In it is written: a son and a daughter inherit equally.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל pushes back with a clear law from the תורה. The philosopher defends his bribed ruling by saying a newer book has replaced the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The philosopher cannot argue with the verse itself, so he claims the whole תורה has been cancelled. 'עוון גליון' is a mocking wordplay on the Greek name of the Christian Gospel, and it literally means 'the sin of the scroll'. His argument is a pretext to justify taking the bribe.

keyTerms.meaning: Where there is a son, the daughter does not inherit
A derisive pun on the name of the Gospel, literally 'the sin of the scroll'

phrases.english: He said to him: It is written for us:
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבן גמליאל, arguing against his own sister's claim.

phrases.english: Where there is a son, a daughter does not inherit.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִן יוֹמָא דִּגְלִיתוּן מֵאַרְעֲכוֹן,
phrases.english: He said to him: From the day you were exiled from your land,
the Torah of Moses was taken away
and the avon gilyon was given,
phrases.notes: This is a mocking wordplay on 'Evangelion', the Gospel.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ: בְּרָא וּבְרַתָּא כַּחֲדָא יִרְתוּן.
phrases.english: and it is written in it: A son and a daughter shall inherit alike.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, כְּתִיב לַן: בִּמְקוֹם בְּרָא, בְּרַתָּא לָא תֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבן גמליאל challenges the ruling from Step 2, and the philosopher defends it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The philosopher claims the תורה was replaced and that son and daughter inherit equally.

steps.title: A bigger bribe, and the philosopher reverses himself
steps.stepSummary: The next day רבן גמליאל gives the philosopher a Libyan donkey. The philosopher now 'discovers' that the עוון גליון itself says it does not change the תורה, so a daughter does not inherit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next day רבן גמליאל, in turn, brought him a Libyan donkey. The philosopher said to them: I read further, to the end of the עוון גליון. It says: I did not come to subtract from the תורה of משה, nor to add to the תורה of משה. And in the תורה is written: where there is a son, the daughter does not inherit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל gives a more valuable bribe, and the philosopher flips his ruling the very next day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The philosopher now quotes the same book against his own ruling of the day before. That book says it does not change the תורה, so the תורה's law stands. The only thing that changed was the size of the bribe, which proves he can be bought.

keyTerms.meaning: A Libyan donkey, an especially valuable animal
I went down to its end, meaning I read further

phrases.english: The next day, in turn, brought him
phrases.notes: This time the giver is רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: he himself, a Libyan donkey.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: שְׁפִילִית לְסֵיפֵיהּ דַּעֲווֹן גִּלְיוֹן,
phrases.english: He said to them: I proceeded to the end of the avon gilyon,
and it is written in it: I did not, to subtract
from the Torah of Moses, come
[and not] to add to the Torah of Moses did I come,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ: בִּמְקוֹם בְּרָא — בְּרַתָּא לָא תֵּירוֹת.
phrases.english: and it is written there: Where there is a son, the daughter does not inherit.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָחָר הֲדַר עַיֵּיל לֵיהּ אִיהוּ חֲמָרָא לוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the ruling of Steps 2 and 3 after a larger bribe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bribed again, the philosopher now rules that the daughter does not inherit.

steps.title: The lamp and the donkey: the punchline
steps.stepSummary: אימא שלום hints at her lamp, and רבן גמליאל answers that the donkey kicked the lamp. This exposes both bribes.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: May your light shine like a lamp. רבן גמליאל said to him: The donkey came and kicked over the lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with two clever lines that reveal the whole trick. Each judgment was bought by a bribe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her line reminds the philosopher of her golden lamp. רבן גמליאל's reply means that his bigger bribe, the donkey, beat her smaller one. The 'incorruptible' judge is fully exposed.

keyTerms.meaning: May your light shine like a lamp

steps.whatToRemember: The story shows that the philosopher's 'honesty' and his 'new law' were both fake. His ruling followed whoever paid more.

phrases.english: She said to him: May your light shine like a lamp.
phrases.notes: This hints at the golden lamp she gave him.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said to him:
The donkey came and kicked the lamp.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: נְהוֹר נְהוֹרָיךְ כִּשְׁרָגָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story by tying together the lamp (Step 1) and the donkey (Step 4).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The philosopher was exposed as taking bribes, and his rulings were for sale.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רב limits the ban to study hours
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's reason that we do not read כתובים on שבת because it takes people away from the בית המדרש. רב says this applies only during the hours of the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: Why do we not read כתובים on שבת? Because of ביטול בית המדרש. רב said: This was taught only for the time when the בית המדרש is in session. When it is not in session, one may read them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the story and goes back to analyzing the משנה. רב gives a first limit on the משנה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's reason is that people would read כתובים instead of going to the שבת lecture. רב reasons that if no lecture is happening, nothing is lost, so reading is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The Writings, the third section of תנ"ך
Taking people away from attending the study hall
They only taught this rule in the case of
During the hours when the study hall is in session

steps.confusionAlert: This rule is about reading כתובים privately on שבת. It is not about saving them from a fire, which is the main topic of the פרק.

phrases.english: And why does one not read, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The answer there is: because of ביטול בית המדרש.

phrases.english: Rav said: They only taught this
during the time of the study hall,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַן בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ — קוֹרִין.
phrases.english: but when it is not the time of the study hall, one may read.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין קוֹרִין כּוּ׳. אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה after the story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, reading כתובים is forbidden only during study-hall hours.

steps.title: שמואל: even outside study hours, no reading
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees and forbids reading כתובים on שבת even when the בית המדרש is not in session.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Even when it is not the time of the בית המדרש, one may not read.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the opposing view. He holds the משנה's ban applies at all times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, the rule is a general ban on שבת, not limited to the hours of the lecture. This sets up the challenge that comes next.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: Even

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַן בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ אֵין קוֹרִין.
phrases.english: when it is not the time of the study hall, one may not read.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַן בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ אֵין קוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues against רב's view in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל (first version), reading כתובים is forbidden at all times on שבת.

steps.title: Challenge from the practice in שמואל's own town
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: in נהרדעא, his own town, they read from כתובים on שבת afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? נהרדעא was שמואל's place, and in נהרדעא they would read a section from כתובים at מנחה time on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first version of שמואל's view. It points out that his own town did not follow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמואל forbids reading כתובים on שבת at all times, his own community would not do so. Yet in נהרדעא they did, at מנחה, which is after study time. This suggests the first version of his view is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that really so? (opens a challenge)
שמואל's place, the town where he was the authority
They would read or conclude a section

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But Neharde'a was Shmuel's place,
and in Neharde'a they would conclude a section in the Writings
at Shabbat afternoon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא נְהַרְדְּעָא אַתְרֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's view from Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that reading is forbidden even outside study hours.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbi's own town would not openly practice against his ruling, yet נהרדעא read כתובים on שבת afternoon.

steps.title: The corrected version: רב depends on location
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-states the מחלוקת. According to רב, the ban applies only in a place where a בית המדרש exists, and elsewhere reading is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if this was said, it was said like this. רב said: This was taught only in a place that has a בית המדרש. In a place without a בית המדרש, one may read.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the whole מחלוקת was quoted wrong, and it gives the correct version, starting with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רב's test is not 'what time is it' but 'is there a בית המדרש here'. If there is no study hall to miss, there is no ביטול, so reading is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said (a corrected version)
In a place where there is a study hall

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the first version רב's test was time (בזמן). In the corrected version רב's test is location (במקום).

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this:
Rav said: They only taught this
in the place of a study hall.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שֶׁלֹּא בִּמְקוֹם בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ — קוֹרִין.
phrases.english: But not in the place of a study hall, one may read.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אִיתְּמַר, הָכִי אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8 by re-stating the מחלוקת, starting with רב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב split by time and שמואל banned reading at all times.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב splits by location. שמואל's view follows in the next step.

steps.title: The corrected version: שמואל depends on time
steps.stepSummary: In the corrected version, שמואל says location does not matter. During study hours reading is forbidden everywhere, and outside study hours it is allowed everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Whether in a place with a בית המדרש or a place without one, during the hours of the בית המדרש one may not read, and outside those hours one may read.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the corrected version with שמואל's view, which now permits reading outside study hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's test is the clock, not the place. Because he now allows reading outside study hours, the challenge from נהרדעא disappears.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: בֵּין בִּמְקוֹם בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: Whether in the place of a study hall
or not in the place of a study hall,
during the time of the study hall, one may not read;
not during the time of the study hall, one may read.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: בֵּין בִּמְקוֹם בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בִּמְקוֹם בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the corrected version begun in Step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל forbade reading even outside study hours.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל forbids reading only during study hours, regardless of location.

steps.title: שמואל is consistent with the practice in נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the corrected view of שמואל fits the practice in נהרדעא of reading כתובים on שבת afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל follows his own reasoning, because in נהרדעא they would read a section from כתובים at מנחה time on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion by showing that the corrected version of שמואל matches what his town actually did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנחה on שבת is after the study session, so reading כתובים then is 'outside study hours'. This is exactly what the corrected שמואל allows. The fact that once challenged him now supports him.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning, he is consistent

steps.whatToRemember: In this corrected version: רב says the ban depends on whether there is a בית המדרש nearby. שמואל says it depends on whether the בית המדרש is in session right now. נהרדעא's reading at מנחה fits שמואל. In the next step, רב אשי offers a different answer.

phrases.english: And Shmuel follows his own reasoning,
for in Neharde'a they would conclude a section of the Writings
at Shabbat afternoon.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַזְדָּא שְׁמוּאֵל לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms that the corrected view in Step 10 fits the fact cited in Step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל allows reading כתובים on שבת outside study hours, as was done in נהרדעא at מנחה.

steps.title: רב אשי keeps the original version and links שמואל to רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the מחלוקת stays as first stated. שמואל forbids reading כתובים on שבת at all times because he follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Really, the dispute is as we said at first, and שמואל holds like רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a different way out of the difficulty. He does not use the corrected version of the מחלוקת. He keeps the original version and says שמואל's strict view comes from רבי נחמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the original version, שמואל forbids reading כתובים on שבת even outside study hours. רב אשי says שמואל was stating this according to רבי נחמיה's reasoning, which the גמרא quotes next. שמואל himself does not hold like רבי נחמיה, so נהרדעא's practice is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; it keeps an earlier position

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Actually, it is as we said at first,
and Shmuel holds like Rabbi Nechemya.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם כְּדַאֲמַרַן מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to the corrected version given in steps 9-11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new source for the opinion (attributes it to a תנא with a different reason)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's view had to be changed so that it allowed reading outside study hours
steps.terutzMaskana: The original version stands. שמואל's ban at all times was stated according to רבי נחמיה's view, not as his own practice, so נהרדעא's reading at מנחה does not contradict him.

steps.title: The ברייתא: no reading, but studying is allowed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that even though we do not read כתבי הקודש on שבת, we may study and explain them, and we may look up a פסוק when we need it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Even though they said we do not read from כתבי הקודש, we may study them and give lectures on them. If someone needs a פסוק, he may bring the book and look in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that contains רבי נחמיה's view. This first part is setting up his statement, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban covers only reading the text straight through. Studying, teaching, and checking a single פסוק are all allowed. This shows the ban is narrow.

keyTerms.meaning: Explain or give a lecture on the text

phrases.english: As it was taught: Even though they said
that we do not read from sacred writings,
we may still study them and give lectures on them.
If he needs a verse, he brings the book and looks in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ כִּתְבֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ אֵין קוֹרִין בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for רב אשי's claim
steps.raayaObject: That there is a תנא whose reason for the ban explains שמואל

steps.title: רבי נחמיה's reason for the ban
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה says the ban exists so that people will conclude that ordinary documents certainly may not be read on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה said: Why did they say we do not read from כתבי הקודש? So that people will say: if we do not read sacred writings, then certainly we do not read ordinary documents.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה explains the reason behind the ban. This reason is what שמואל relies on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נחמיה, the ban is not about getting people to attend the בית המדרש. It is a safeguard so that people will not read business papers on שבת, and that concern exists at every hour. שמואל's ban 'at all times' was said according to רבי נחמיה. שמואל himself does not hold this way, which is why נהרדעא could read כתובים at מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary documents, such as contracts and letters

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, the מחלוקת stays as first stated. שמואל's ban on reading כתובים at all times was said according to רבי נחמיה, whose reason is to keep people from reading ordinary documents. שמואל personally does not follow רבי נחמיה, so the practice in נהרדעא is no contradiction.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya said:
Why did they say
that we do not read from sacred writings?

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּ: בְּכִתְבֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ אֵין קוֹרִין,
phrases.english: So that people will say: if we do not read sacred writings,
then all the more so we do not read ordinary documents.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with רבי נחמיה's reason, which רב אשי says lies behind שמואל's ruling
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ban on reading כתובים at all times

steps.title: משנה: rescuing the case along with the ספר or the תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows rescuing a ספר תורה's case together with the ספר, and a תפילין case together with the תפילין, even if there are coins inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We may rescue the case of a ספר תורה together with the ספר, and the case of תפילין together with the תפילין, even if there are coins inside them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that when we rescue holy items from a fire on שבת, we may take their cases along with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is treated as part of the holy item it holds. Coins inside the case do not stop us from rescuing it, even though coins are usually מוקצה.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ מַצִּילִין תִּיק הַסֵּפֶר עִם הַסֵּפֶר,
phrases.english: MISHNAH: We may rescue the case of the scroll together with the scroll,
and the case of the tefillin together with the tefillin,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּתוֹכָן מָעוֹת.
phrases.english: even if there are coins inside them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַצִּילִין תִּיק הַסֵּפֶר עִם הַסֵּפֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case may be rescued together with the holy item it holds, even if it has coins inside

steps.title: Where they may be carried: closed or open alley
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא allows bringing them only into a closed מבוי. בן בתירא allows even an open one.
steps.simpleTranslation: To where may we rescue them? Into an alley that is not open at both ends. בן בתירא says: even into an open alley.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks where we may carry the rescued items and records a dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מבוי closed on one end is safer in terms of carrying rules. בן בתירא is more lenient and allows even a מבוי open at both ends.

phrases.english: And to where may we rescue them?
Into an alley that is not open at both ends.
Ben Beteira says: Even into an open alley.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְהֵיכָן מַצִּילִין אוֹתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: only a closed מבוי. בן בתירא: even an open מבוי

steps.title: ברייתא: how much of the קרבן פסח may be skinned on שבת
steps.stepSummary: When the fourteenth of ניסן falls on שבת, רבי ישמעאל says we skin the קרבן פסח only down to the chest. The חכמים say we skin all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: When the fourteenth falls on שבת, we skin the פסח down to the chest. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. The חכמים say: we skin all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא with a מחלוקת about skinning the קרבן פסח on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Skinning down to the chest is enough to take out the parts burned on the מזבח. The question is whether we may keep skinning past what the מזבח needs.

keyTerms.meaning: The fourteenth of ניסן, ערב פסח

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
When the fourteenth of Nissan falls on Shabbat,
we skin the Pesach offering down to the chest.

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה.
phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka.
And the Sages say: We skin all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related ברייתא quoted on the topic of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל: skin only to the chest. חכמים: skin the whole animal

steps.title: What is the Rabbis' reason?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל's view makes sense, since the מזבח's need was already met. But why do the רבנן allow skinning the whole animal?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to רבי ישמעאל, since the need of the Most High was already done. But according to the רבנן, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבי ישמעאל's logic and asks for the רבנן's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the parts for the מזבח are out, more skinning seems to serve only the people eating it. So why should it be allowed on שבת?

keyTerms.meaning: The need of the Most High (the מזבח's need)

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה,
phrases.english: It makes sense according to Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka,
since the need of the Most High has already been done.
But according to the Rabbis, what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning of one side of the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the רבנן allowing full skinning on שבת

steps.title: The verse: everything God made is for His sake
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings the פסוק "כל פעל ה' למענהו" as the source for the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Because the פסוק says, "Everything that ה׳ made is for His sake."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק from משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whatever brings honor to ה׳ counts as His need. So full skinning can be part of what is done "for His sake".

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Because the verse says:
"Everything that ה׳ made is for His sake."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question

steps.title: How is skinning here for His sake?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what honor to ה׳ there is in skinning the rest of the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, what "for His sake" is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the פסוק fits this case. This sets up two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is general. The גמרא wants to know exactly how skinning the rest of the hide honors ה׳.

phrases.english: And here, what "for His sake" is there?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכָא, מַאי ״לְמַעֲנֵהוּ״ אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the פסוק applies

steps.title: Two answers: so it won't spoil, or so it won't be disgraced
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says it is so the meat will not rot. רבא says it is so holy offerings will not lie around like a נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: so that it will not rot. רבא said: so that holy offerings will not be left lying like a carcass.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים explain how full skinning is "for His sake".
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף focuses on protecting the meat from spoiling. רבא focuses on the respect owed to a holy offering, which should not look like an abandoned carcass.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: So that it will not rot.
Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ קׇדְשֵׁי שָׁמַיִם מוּטָלִין כִּנְבֵלָה.
phrases.english: So that holy offerings will not be left lying like a carcass.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: שֶׁלֹּא יַסְרִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף: to prevent rotting. רבא: to prevent disgrace

steps.title: What is the practical difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what case the two explanations would lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רב יוסף and רבא would rule differently. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually both concerns are present at the same time. The גמרא looks for a case where only one of them applies.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference between the two answers
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where only one concern applies

steps.title: A golden table, or a cold north-wind day
steps.stepSummary: On a golden table there is no disgrace, but it can still rot. On a cold north-wind day it will not rot, but it is still disgraced.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference when it is placed on a golden table, or on a day with a cold north wind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two cases where the two explanations lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a golden table only רב יוסף's concern of rotting applies. On a cold day only רבא's concern of disgrace applies.

keyTerms.meaning: A day with a cold north wind

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
when it is placed on a golden table,
or on a day with a cold north wind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּמַנַּח אַפָּתוּרָא דְּדַהֲבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Golden table: only rotting applies. Cold day: only disgrace applies

steps.title: How does רבי ישמעאל use the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי ישמעאל learns from "פעל ה' למענהו", since he does not use it to allow full skinning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, what does he do with "ה׳ made for His sake"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to רבי ישמעאל and asks how he uses the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי ישמעאל does not learn full skinning from the פסוק, it should still teach him something.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it (how does he use it)?

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי ״פָּעַל ה׳ לַמַּעֲנֵהוּ״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: what does he do with this "ה׳ made for His sake"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה, הַאי ״פָּעַל ה׳ לַמַּעֲנֵהוּ״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the other side of the מחלוקת
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי ישמעאל learns from the פסוק

steps.title: Do not remove the altar parts before skinning
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל learns from the פסוק that we must not take out the אימורין before removing the hide. That is why he allows partial skinning.
steps.simpleTranslation: That one may not take out the אימורין before skinning the hide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי ישמעאל uses the פסוק to require skinning before the parts for the מזבח are removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the פסוק, we could cut a hole in the hide and pull the אימורין out with no skinning at all. The פסוק requires skinning first, so the skinning down to the chest is allowed on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The parts of the offering burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: That one may not take out the sacrificial parts
before skinning the hide.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא יוֹצִיא אֶת הָאֵימוּרִין קוֹדֶם הַפְשָׁטַת הָעוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches that skinning must come before removing the אימורין

steps.title: Why must skinning come first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the אימורין cannot be taken out before skinning.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind this rule. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not obvious why pulling the parts out through a hole would be a problem, so the גמרא asks.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in step 25
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the אימורין may not come out before skinning

steps.title: Because of the hairs
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא son of רב נתן says the reason is the hairs, which would stick to the אימורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב נתן said: Because of the hairs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason: pulling the parts out through the hide would leave hairs on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hairs stuck on the אימורין would make them look bad when offered to ה׳. This is the honor "for His sake" that רבי ישמעאל sees in skinning first.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use "כל פעל ה' למענהו". The רבנן use it to allow skinning the whole animal. רבי ישמעאל uses it to require skinning before removing the אימורין, because of the hairs.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Natan said:
Because of the hairs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן: מִשּׁוּם נִימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Hairs would stick to the אימורין and spoil their appearance

steps.title: What did the group answer רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting מר עוקבא, asks what argument the group gave to רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of מר עוקבא: What did the group answer to רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks what reasoning the group gave in their exchange with רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה about skinning the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא explained the reasoning of רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, who allows only partial skinning. Now it asks how his colleagues, the חכמים who allow skinning the whole animal, argued against him. The next step gives their argument, which is drawn from our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: They answered him / replied to him
The group of colleagues / fellow scholars (here, the חכמים who argued with him)

steps.confusionAlert: The רבי ישמעאל in steps 17–27 is this same רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, who allows skinning only down to the chest. The 'group' (חבריא) are his colleagues on the side of the רבנן, who argued against him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Mar Ukva said:
What did the group of colleagues answer

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה?
phrases.english: to Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אַהְדַּרוּ לֵיהּ חַבְרַיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the reasoning of רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, the גמרא turns to the argument his colleagues made against him.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What logical argument did the group make in this exchange?

steps.title: The comparison to saving a ספר תורה casing
steps.stepSummary: The group argued that if we may save the casing together with the ספר תורה, we should be allowed to skin the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they said to him: If we may save the casing of the ספר together with the ספר, should we not skin the פסח of its hide?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the group's argument. It compares skinning the פסח to the rule in our משנה that we may save a ספר תורה together with its casing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is that something secondary may come along with something important. The casing is saved because of the ספר. In the same way, once part of the skinning is already allowed, the rest of the skinning should be allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: We save / rescue (from a fire on שבת)
The casing of the ספר תורה
We will skin / strip off the hide

phrases.english: This is what they said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִם מַצִּילִין תִּיק הַסֵּפֶר עִם הַסֵּפֶר,
phrases.english: If we save the casing of the scroll along with the scroll,
should we not strip the Paschal lamb of its hide?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28 by giving the group's argument.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argued from the rule that a ספר תורה casing is saved along with the ספר, so the skinning of the פסח should be allowed as well.

steps.title: The two cases are not alike: moving versus labor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that saving the casing only involves moving, while skinning is a real forbidden labor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they comparable?! There, it is only moving. Here, it is a forbidden labor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison. It says the two cases are too different to learn one from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saving the casing only involves טלטול, moving an object, which is a light rabbinic prohibition. Skinning an animal is a real מלאכה, forbidden by the תורה. A leniency about moving cannot prove a leniency about a labor forbidden by the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it comparable?! (a way of rejecting a comparison)
Moving an object (a rabbinic prohibition on שבת)
A forbidden creative labor on שבת (a prohibition from the תורה)

steps.confusionAlert: Skinning is a real מלאכה, forbidden by the תורה. Moving the casing is only טלטול, which is a much lighter prohibition. That difference is the whole point of this challenge.

phrases.english: Are they comparable?!
There, it is moving,
here, it is a forbidden labor!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison made in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between saving the ספר תורה casing and skinning the פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A leniency about טלטול (rabbinic) cannot teach a leniency about a מלאכה (from the תורה).

steps.title: רב אשי: the dispute has two parts, and the comparison was about moving
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that they disagree about both moving and labor. The casing comparison was only used for moving the hide along with the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: They disagree about two things. They disagree about moving, and they disagree about labor. This is what they said to him: If we may save the casing of the ספר together with the ספר, should we not move the hide along with the meat?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. He explains that the ספר תורה casing comparison was never about the labor of skinning. It was about moving the hide together with the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate issues in the dispute. The first is whether the skinning (מלאכה) is allowed. The second is whether the hide may be moved along with the meat (טלטול). The comparison to the casing fits the moving issue perfectly, since both cases are about moving a secondary item along with a main item, so the challenge of step 30 falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Along with / by means of (something else)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, the חכמים' comparison to the ספר תורה casing was only about טלטול: just as the casing is saved along with the ספר, the hide should be moved along with the meat. Whether the skinning itself (מלאכה) is allowed is a separate point in their dispute with רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches an important rule of method. A proof is only valid for the same kind of prohibition. A comparison about moving can prove something about moving, but not about labor.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
They disagree about two things:
they disagree about moving
and they disagree about the labor,
and this is what they said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִם מַצִּילִין תִּיק הַסֵּפֶר עִם הַסֵּפֶר,
phrases.english: If we save the casing of the scroll along with the scroll,
should we not move the hide along with the meat?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: בְּתַרְתֵּי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 30 by narrowing the comparison to the issue of moving.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope: the comparison applies only to טלטול, not to מלאכה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ספר תורה casing comparison was meant to allow the labor of skinning, which would make it a weak comparison.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison only allows moving the hide along with the meat. The labor question is a separate part of the dispute.
